To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

The microbial community of the windrow composting process is characterized by a rapid succession of functional microbial communities, which is affected by temperature peaks and the timing of the mild thermophillic phase.
the composting process is a complex process with several stages that are characterized by specific abiotic and biotic conditions.

(i) the pH, C/N and VS content, O(2) concentration in the pile, and CO(2), CH(4) and NH(3) gas emissions correlated with composting time; (ii) the microbial succession of total and thermophilic mesophilic bacteria, fungi and E. coli correlated with composting stage; (iii) the microbial succession in the thermophilic and post-thermophilic stages correlated with temperature and temperature decline;
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a biowaste treatment system in Crete, based on windrow composting.
the characterization of the composting process of biowaste in the Mediterranean climate of Crete and the microbial populations involved.
the microbial succession in the composting of biodegradable municipal waste and the correlation of the microbial counts with the abiotic parameters and the composting process.

the composting process was completed after 2 months of operation.
the microbial population in compost is a function of the abiotic conditions in the composting environment, the temperature regime and the duration of the process.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the thermophilic period in composting, as well as its peak temperature and duration, affect the microbial population dynamics and the quality of the end product.
the composting of biodegradable waste in windrows in Crete, under the climatic conditions prevailing in the area, is a feasible process that can be used as an alternative to land filling.
the composting process is not a single process but rather a combination of processes, each with its own specific characteristics.
The main takeaway from our work is that

composting of source-segregated biowaste in windrows is an efficient process for the production of mature compost, and that the process can be monitored by the use of simple abiotic and microbial parameters.
the microbial groups examined in the study are not good indicators of the composting process.

, although the composting process is highly dynamic and the succession of microbial groups is complex and difficult to predict, the temperature profile of the composting process and its correlation with other abiotic factors is a useful tool for the monitoring and control of the process.
